summary_ja: 自己資本比率規制金融機関向けエクスポージャーのリスク・ウェイトを、格付がある場合は信用リスク区分、無格付の場合はグレード区分（A・B・C）により定め、短期・貿易関連の軽減、暗黙の政府支援を勘案しない格付の使用、グレード判定要件、高い自己資本の場合の三十パーセント適用等を規定する。
summary_en: Risk weights for exposures to regulated financial institutions: by rating where rated (no implicit government support), by grade A/B/C where unrated, with lower weights for short-term and trade exposures, the tests for each grade, and 30% for grade-A banks with CET1 ≥ 14% and leverage ≥ 5%.

terms.ja: 金融機関向けエクスポージャー

paragraphs: For exposures to capital-regulated financial institutions (meaning financial institutions subject to the capital adequacy standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards (excluding persons listed in Article 1, item (vii)(b)), foreign banks, bank holding companies, foreign companies equivalent to bank holding companies, or securities finance companies (meaning securities finance companies provided in Article 2, paragraph (30) of the Act; the same applies in Article 77, paragraph (2), item (ii) and Article 81, paragraph (2), item (ii)); the same applies hereinafter) (referred to as "exposures to financial institutions" in this Article and in Article 33, paragraphs (1) and (4)), the risk weight where there is a rating shall be as set out in the left column of the following table, according to the credit risk category corresponding to that rating. {{T:p60t0}}

The risk weight of exposures to which a risk weight of 30%, 50% or 100% applies under the preceding paragraph and which fall under either of the following items may be as set out in the left column of the following table, according to the risk weight applied under that paragraph. In this case, the risk weight of the exposure to financial institutions referred to shall be a value reflecting the results of the due diligence analysis provided in paragraph (4). {{T:p61t1}} (i) Exposures to financial institutions whose period from the date credit was extended to maturity is three months or less. (ii) Exposures to financial institutions relating to trade transactions for which the period provided in the preceding item is six months or less (including highly liquid trade-related contingent liabilities, and excluding those listed in that item).

Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach uses ratings under paragraph (1), it shall use ratings that do not take into account implicit government support (meaning the possibility that, where there is a risk of extremely serious disruption to the maintenance of credit order in a country or region, measures taken with respect to financial institutions under laws and regulations (including foreign laws and regulations) or similar measures (excluding measures that make only the shareholders or creditors of the financial institution bear losses) may be taken with respect to the capital-regulated financial institution).

In paragraph (1), where, as a result of the due diligence analysis by the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach, the credit standing of a capital-regulated financial institution is assessed as carrying higher risk than the credit standing indicated by the credit risk category corresponding to its rating, the risk weight corresponding to a credit risk category one or more grades lower than the credit risk category corresponding to that rating shall be used; provided, however, that a risk weight corresponding to a credit risk category higher than the credit risk category corresponding to that rating shall not be used.

Where exposures to financial institutions are unrated, their risk weight shall be as set out in the left column of the following table, according to the grade of the capital-regulated financial institution (meaning the category of credit risk assessment for exposures to financial institutions where the capital-regulated financial institution is unrated; the same applies hereinafter in this Article) determined under the provisions of paragraphs (7), (9) and (10). {{T:p61t2}}

The risk weight of exposures to which a risk weight of 40% or 75% applies under the preceding paragraph and which fall under either item of paragraph (2) may be as set out in the left column of the following table, according to the risk weight applied under the preceding paragraph. {{T:p62t1}}

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall determine the grade of a capital-regulated financial institution that satisfies all of the following requirements to be A. (i) That it has the capacity to meet its obligations in accordance with its contracts, and is expected to continue to maintain that capacity even if economic conditions or the business environment deteriorate. (ii) That it satisfies the requirements specified in (a) through (p) below, according to the category of capital-regulated financial institution listed in (a) through (p). (a) An internationally active bank as provided in Article 1, item (x-2) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 14-2 of the Banking Act, whether a bank's capital adequacy is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that it holds (FSA Notice No. 19 of 2006; "Bank Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 2 and Article 14 of the Bank Capital Adequacy Notice, and the standards other than those minimum standards set out in Article 2-2, paragraph (1) and Article 14-2, paragraph (1) of the same Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the standards for determining soundness relating to leverage, set as a complementary indicator to the Bank Capital Adequacy Notice (FSA Notice No. 11 of 2019; "Bank Leverage Notice"), and the standard other than that minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (2) of the same Notice (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice). (b) An internationally active bank as provided in Article 1, item (x-2) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 52-25 of the Banking Act, whether the capital adequacy of a bank holding company and its subsidiaries is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that they hold (FSA Notice No. 20 of 2006; "Bank Holding Company Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standard set out in Article 2 of the Bank Holding Company Capital Adequacy Notice, and the standard other than that minimum standard set out in Article 2-2, paragraph (1) of the same Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) of the standards for determining soundness relating to leverage, set as a complementary indicator to the Bank Holding Company Capital Adequacy Notice (FSA Notice No. 12 of 2019; "Bank Holding Company Leverage Notice"), and the standard other than that minimum standard set out in paragraph (2) of the same Article. (c) An internationally active shinkin bank as provided in Article 1, item (ix-3) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 14-2 of the Banking Act as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 89, paragraph (1) of the Shinkin Bank Act, whether the capital adequacy of shinkin banks and federations of shinkin banks is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that they hold (FSA Notice No. 21 of 2006; "Shinkin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 19 and Article 31 of the Shinkin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice, and the standards other than those minimum standards set out in Article 19-2, paragraph (1) and Article 31-2, paragraph (1) of the same Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the standards for determining soundness relating to leverage, set as a complementary indicator to the Shinkin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice (FSA Notice No. 14 of 2019; "Shinkin Bank Leverage Notice"), and the standard other than that minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (2) of the same Notice (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice). (d) The Norinchukin Bank: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 2 and Article 14 of the standards for the Norinchukin Bank to determine the soundness of its management (FSA/MAFF Notice No. 4 of 2006; "Norinchukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice"), and the standards other than those minimum standards set out in Article 2-2, paragraph (1) and Article 14-2, paragraph (1) of the same Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the standards for determining soundness relating to leverage, set as a complementary indicator to the Norinchukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice (FSA/MAFF Notice No. 4 of 2019; "Norinchukin Bank Leverage Notice"), and the standard other than that minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (2) of the same Notice (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice). (e) The Shoko Chukin Bank, Ltd.: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 2 and Article 14 of the standards for the Shoko Chukin Bank, Ltd. to determine the soundness of its management pursuant to Article 23, paragraph (1) of the Shoko Chukin Bank Limited Act (FSA/MOF/METI Notice No. 2 of 2008; "Shoko Chukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice"), and the standards other than those minimum standards set out in Article 2-2, paragraph (1) and Article 14-2, paragraph (1) of the same Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the standards for determining soundness relating to leverage, set as a complementary indicator to the Shoko Chukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice (FSA/MOF/METI Notice No. 3 of 2019; "Shoko Chukin Bank Leverage Notice"), and the standard other than that minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (2) of the same Notice (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice). (f) A foreign bank (limited to one equivalent to an internationally active bank provided in (a)): it satisfies standards similar to those listed in (a)(1) and (2) (including standards specific to that foreign bank set by each country (limited to those that have been published)). (g) A foreign company equivalent to a bank holding company (limited to one equivalent to an internationally active bank provided in (b)): it satisfies standards similar to those listed in (b)(1) and (2) (including standards specific to that foreign company set by each country (limited to those that have been published)). (h) A domestic standard bank as provided in Article 1, item (x-3) of the Bank Capital Adequacy Notice: it satisfies the standards set out in Article 25 and Article 37 of the same Notice. (i) A domestic standard bank as provided in Article 1, item (x-3) of the Bank Holding Company Capital Adequacy Notice: it satisfies the standard set out in Article 14 of the same Notice. (j) A domestic standard shinkin bank as provided in Article 1, item (ix-2) of the Shinkin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice: it satisfies the standards set out in Article 2 and Article 11 of the same Notice. (k) A credit cooperative, etc. as provided in Article 1, item (ii) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 14-2 of the Banking Act as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 6, paragraph (1) of the Act on Financial Businesses by Cooperatives, whether the capital adequacy of credit cooperatives and federations of credit cooperatives is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that they hold (FSA Notice No. 22 of 2006; "the Credit Cooperative Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies the standards set out in Article 2 and Article 11 of the same Notice. (l) A labour bank as provided in Article 1, item (vii-3) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 14-2 of the Banking Act as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 94, paragraph (1) of the Labour Bank Act, whether the capital adequacy of labour banks and federations of labour banks is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that they hold (FSA/MHLW Notice No. 7 of 2006; "the Labour Bank Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies the standards set out in Article 2 and Article 11 of the same Notice. (m) A cooperative as provided in Article 1, item (vii)(d) of the standards for agricultural cooperatives, etc. to determine the soundness of their management (FSA/MAFF Notice No. 2 of 2006; "the Agricultural Cooperative Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies the standards set out in Article 2 and Article 10 of the same Notice. (n) A cooperative as provided in Article 1, item (vii)(e) of the standards for fishery cooperatives, etc. to determine the soundness of their management (FSA/MAFF Notice No. 3 of 2006; "the Fishery Cooperative Capital Adequacy Notice"): it satisfies the standards set out in Article 2 and Article 10 of the same Notice. (o) A foreign bank (limited to one equivalent to a domestic standard bank provided in (h)): it satisfies standards similar to those provided in (h) (including standards specific to that foreign bank set by each country (limited to those that have been published)). (p) A foreign company equivalent to a bank holding company (limited to one equivalent to a domestic standard bank provided in (i)): it satisfies standards similar to those provided in (i) (including standards specific to that foreign company set by each country (limited to those that have been published)). (iii) That information necessary for the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach to confirm that the capital-regulated financial institution satisfies the requirements listed in the preceding item has been published, or that such information is appropriately provided to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach.

Notwithstanding the provisions of paragraph (5), where the grade of a capital-regulated financial institution (limited to one falling under any of item (ii)(a) through (g) of the preceding paragraph) is determined to be A under the preceding paragraph, and it satisfies the requirement specified in each of the following items according to the category of capital-regulated financial institution listed in that item, the risk weight of exposures to that capital-regulated financial institution may be 30%. (i) An internationally active bank provided in item (ii)(a) of the preceding paragraph: the ratio obtained by the formulas of Article 2, item (i) and Article 14, item (i) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 14-2 of the Banking Act, whether a bank's capital adequacy is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that it holds (referred to as the "Common Equity Tier 1 ratio" in item (vi)) is 14% or more, and the ratio obtained by the formula of Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis with the necessary replacement of terms under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Bank Leverage Notice (referred to as the "leverage ratio" in item (vi)) is 5% or more. (ii) An internationally active bank provided in item (ii)(b) of the preceding paragraph: the ratio obtained by the formula of Article 2, item (i) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 52-25 of the Banking Act, whether the capital adequacy of a bank holding company and its subsidiaries is appropriate in light of the assets, etc. that they hold (referred to as the "Common Equity Tier 1 ratio" in item (vii)) is 14% or more, and the ratio obtained by the formula of Article 2, paragraph (1) of the Bank Holding Company Leverage Notice (referred to as the "leverage ratio" in item (vii)) is 5% or more. (iii) An internationally active shinkin bank provided in item (ii)(c) of the preceding paragraph: the ratio obtained by the formulas of Article 19, item (i) and Article 31, item (i) of the standards for determining, pursuant to Article 14-2 of the Banking Act as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 89, paragraph (1) of the Shinkin Bank Act, whether the capital adequacy of shinkin banks and federations of shinkin banks is appropriate is 14% or more, and the ratio obtained by the formula of Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis with the necessary replacement of terms under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Shinkin Bank Leverage Notice is 5% or more. (iv) The Norinchukin Bank: the ratio obtained by the formulas of Article 2, item (i) and Article 14, item (i) of the Norinchukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice is 14% or more, and the ratio obtained by the formula of Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis with the necessary replacement of terms under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Norinchukin Bank Leverage Notice is 5% or more. (v) The Shoko Chukin Bank, Ltd.: the ratio obtained by the formulas of Article 2, item (i) and Article 14, item (i) of the standards for the Shoko Chukin Bank, Ltd. to determine the soundness of its management pursuant to Article 23, paragraph (1) of the Shoko Chukin Bank Limited Act is 14% or more, and the ratio obtained by the formula of Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis with the necessary replacement of terms under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Shoko Chukin Bank Leverage Notice is 5% or more. (vi) A foreign bank (limited to one equivalent to an internationally active bank provided in item (ii)(a) of the preceding paragraph): a ratio similar to the Common Equity Tier 1 ratio, calculated under the capital adequacy standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards, is 14% or more, and a ratio similar to the leverage ratio, calculated under the leverage ratio standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards, is 5% or more. (vii) A foreign company equivalent to a bank holding company (limited to one equivalent to an internationally active bank provided in item (ii)(b) of the preceding paragraph): a ratio similar to the Common Equity Tier 1 ratio, calculated under the capital adequacy standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards, is 14% or more, and a ratio similar to the leverage ratio, calculated under the leverage ratio standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards, is 5% or more.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall determine the grade of a capital-regulated financial institution that satisfies all of the following requirements (excluding one whose grade has been determined to be A under paragraph (7) and those listed in item (ii)(h) through (p) of that paragraph) to be B. (i) That, as of the calculation reference date, no doubt has arisen as to its capacity to meet its obligations. (ii) That it satisfies the requirements specified in (a) through (g) below, according to the category of capital-regulated financial institution listed in (a) through (g). (a) An internationally active bank as provided in Article 1, item (x-2) of the Bank Capital Adequacy Notice: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 2 and Article 14 of the Bank Capital Adequacy Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Bank Leverage Notice. (b) An internationally active bank as provided in Article 1, item (x-2) of the Bank Holding Company Capital Adequacy Notice: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standard set out in Article 2 of the Bank Holding Company Capital Adequacy Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) of the Bank Holding Company Leverage Notice. (c) An internationally active shinkin bank as provided in Article 1, item (ix-3) of the Shinkin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 19 and Article 31 of the Shinkin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Shinkin Bank Leverage Notice. (d) The Norinchukin Bank: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 2 and Article 14 of the Norinchukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Norinchukin Bank Leverage Notice. (e) The Shoko Chukin Bank, Ltd.: it satisfies all of the following standards. (1) The minimum standards set out in Article 2 and Article 14 of the Shoko Chukin Bank Capital Adequacy Notice. (2) The minimum standard set out in Article 2, paragraph (1) (including where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 5, paragraph (1) of the same Notice) of the Shoko Chukin Bank Leverage Notice. (f) A foreign bank (limited to one equivalent to an internationally active bank provided in (a)): it satisfies standards similar to those listed in (a)(1) and (2). (g) A foreign company equivalent to a bank holding company (limited to one equivalent to an internationally active bank provided in (b)): it satisfies standards similar to those listed in (b)(1) and (2). (iii) That information necessary for the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach to confirm that the capital-regulated financial institution satisfies the requirements listed in the preceding item has been published, or that such information is appropriately provided to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach shall determine the grade of a capital-regulated financial institution falling under any of the following items (excluding one whose grade has been determined to be A under paragraph (7) and one whose grade has been determined to be B under the preceding paragraph) to be C. (i) Where, as of the calculation reference date, there is doubt as to its capacity to meet its obligations, or it is already unable to meet its obligations. (ii) Where the capital adequacy standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards applicable to the capital-regulated financial institution have not been set by the financial authority of the country or region in which it was established. (iii) Where the capital adequacy standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards applicable to the capital-regulated financial institution have been set by the financial authority of the country or region in which it was established, and it does not satisfy those standards. (iv) Where the capital adequacy standards set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision or similar standards applicable to the capital-regulated financial institution have been set by the financial authority of the country or region in which it was established, and the information necessary for the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach to confirm that it satisfies those standards has not been published and is not appropriately provided to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach. (v) Where an audit of the capital-regulated financial institution by an external auditor is required under the laws and regulations of the country or region in which it is located, and within the past twelve months either of the following has occurred: (a) An adverse opinion has been expressed by the external auditor in the audit report on the financial statements. (b) Substantial doubt about the going-concern assumption in the financial statements has been expressed by the external auditor (including where a note on the going-concern assumption has been made in the financial statements). (vi) Where its grade has not been determined to be A under paragraph (7) and has not been determined to be B under the preceding paragraph.

Where the risk weight according to the grade provided in paragraphs (5), (6) and (8) is used, the risk weight of an exposure to financial institutions that meets all of the following requirements shall not be lower than the risk weight provided in Article 22 for the central government of the country or region in which the capital-regulated financial institution that is the counterparty of that exposure was established; provided, however, that this shall not apply to exposures to financial institutions whose period from the date the capital-regulated financial institution received the credit to maturity is less than one year and that relate to highly liquid trade-related contingent liabilities. (i) That it is denominated in a currency different from the local currency of the country or region in which the capital-regulated financial institution was established. (ii) That it is booked in an office located in a country or region different from the one in which the capital-regulated financial institution was established, and is denominated in a currency different from the local currency of the country or region in which that office is located.
